label: Plato, Theaetetus 171a-c: The unqualified doctrine fails: not every opined content in scope is…
interpretation: Socrates' "most exquisite" point: granting the deniers' opinion to be true, Protagoras would concede his own to be false; the deniers do not concede they are wrong; so the doctrine is disputed by all, Protagoras included, and his Truth is true for no one (171c). Unqualified reading: with "true" and "false" unindexed, the doctrine refutes itself. Formalized as horn 1, conditional on the scope premise and on unindexed truth respecting negation (STMT-PILOT-NEGATION-RESPECTED, an open bridge). Whether Plato's dropped qualifiers are a fallacy or a deliberate argument is a scholarly question this claim does not decide.
